mathematical_or_operational_scope: Recursive 16:46 source ZIP provenance and extracted-byte consistency audit.
positive_controls: Lines 17–24 reject absolute/traversal member paths and archive symlinks and compare decompressed bytes to extracted files.
Lines 28–34 validate each encountered SHA256SUMS entry exactly; lines 37–40 compare a freshly observed inventory with a prior inventory.

findings.issue: No recursion-depth, member-count, expansion-size or cumulative-memory caps. ZIP detection uses only a local-file-header prefix and misses ZIP variants such as empty/self-extracting archives.

Duplicate member names overwrite the members dictionary, and the final inventory comparison uses sets, discarding duplicate occurrence multiplicity. These checks do not prove exact sequence/multiplicity identity.
Extracted-file checking follows filesystem symlinks without asserting containment of resolved paths. Archive-side symlink rejection alone does not validate the preexisting extracted tree.
Missing or empty recognized manifests pass vacuously and still yield all_manifest_hashes_pass=True. Checks cover manifest-listed entries, not required coverage of every member.
All rejection gates are assertions and disappear under optimized Python.

cost_and_scaling: O(B) hash/read work for decompressed bytes, with nested in-memory ZIP recursion and repeated extracted-tree reads. No explicit resource bounds.
test_scope_and_limits: No execution. Source performs runtime inventory/manifest assertions but has no hostile-archive regression suite or fail-closed minimum counts.
certificate_acceptance: Establishes byte agreement only for observed inputs under its path/manifest conventions. It is not an authenticated signature, mathematical review, or robust adversarial archive validator.
